scope: External source-evidence acquisition pass for six prioritized FMO candidates only. The pass evaluates source strength, public identifiers, duplicate risk, and source-only disposition before any source-free geometry or review-packet work.

public_source_systems_accessed.purpose: review status, protein names, FAD cofactor annotations, catalytic activities, Rhea cross-references, PDB cross-references, and AlphaFold cross-references
reaction identifiers carried by UniProt catalytic activity records
public PDB titles, methods, resolutions, and observed nonpolymer cofactors where available
public AlphaFold model identifiers, version, and model file URLs
primary and review source abstracts or open full text for cofactor, reductive activation, and C4a/peroxyflavin mechanism evidence

local_artifacts_inspected.role: prior broad source scout and source-admissible candidate list
duplicate, family-overlap, hard-negative, and leakage gate for the same six external candidates
local proposed FMO context for m_csa:551 and m_csa:973
prior source-free geometry and duplicate/leakage terminal context for O15229 and H3JQW0

summary.bottom_line: All six candidates have source evidence for flavin monooxygenase chemistry. CHMO, HAPMO, and human FMO1 are clean source-only leads for later source-free structure/geometry and review packets. OTEMO, KMO, and salicylate 1-monooxygenase are held despite positive source chemistry because duplicate, leakage, or same-family boundary risks dominate this acquisition pass.

rhea.reaction: cyclohexanone + NADPH + O2 + H(+) = hexano-6-lactone + NADP(+) + H2O

candidate_packets.fad_fmn_cofactor_evidence: UniProt records FAD as the cofactor with experimental evidence from PMID:1261545 and PMID:7093214 and notes one FAD per subunit. PMID:1261545 reports the purified Acinetobacter cyclohexanone oxygenase contains one bound FAD per enzyme molecule.

nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.evidence: UniProt/Rhea records an NADPH-consuming cyclohexanone + O2 reaction and UniProt states CHMO cannot use NADH. PMID:7093214 describes O2 reduction at the expense of NADPH during oxygen transfer to substrate.
nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.two_component_distinction: No partner reductase or diffusible reduced-flavin supply is required in the reviewed source context; this is a self-contained FAD/NADPH oxygenase, not a reductase-only enzyme.

candidate_packets.o2_derived_substrate_oxygen_insertion_ev: UniProt records conversion of cyclohexanone to epsilon-caprolactone by inserting oxygen into the ring and explicitly notes a detectable FAD-4a-OOH transient intermediate. PMID:7093214 reports a 4a-hydroperoxyflavin intermediate during catalysis and supports Baeyer-Villiger oxygen insertion.

duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:131: low; CHMO is carbonyl Baeyer-Villiger lactone formation, not 4-hydroxybenzoate aromatic hydroxylation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:132: low; CHMO is a single-component FAD/NADPH BVMO, not FMNH2 alkanal luciferase chemistry.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:551: low; CHMO is not phenol ortho hydroxylation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:973: low; CHMO is not a two-component reduced-FMN sulfur monooxygenase.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.external_family_overlap: Broad BVMO overlap with HAPMO and OTEMO, but CHMO is the top-priority BVMO source lead and adds the clean carbonyl/lactone oxygen-insertion axis.

not_other_family_rationale.not_ordinary_flavin_dehydrogenase_reduct: The source product is an oxygen-inserted lactone and not a dehydrogenation product or carrier-reduction endpoint.
not_other_family_rationale.not_oxidase_only: O2-derived oxygen is inserted into substrate; O2 is not only a terminal electron acceptor.
not_other_family_rationale.not_fe_s_relay_or_reductase_only: No Fe-S relay or partner-only reductase role is invoked; FAD/NADPH oxygenation occurs in the CHMO enzyme.
not_other_family_rationale.not_heme_p450_pterin_metal_copper: Reviewed sources identify FAD/NADPH BVMO chemistry, with no heme, P450, pterin, non-heme iron, copper, or diiron oxygenase evidence.
not_other_family_rationale.not_name_only: The evidence includes FAD, NADPH, O2, lactone product, and a 4a-hydroperoxyflavin intermediate.

candidate_packets.disposition_reason: Strong candidate-specific source evidence and low duplicate risk against current M-CSA FMO rows. Carry forward only to source-free structure/geometry and review-packet work; make no countable label claim.

candidate_packets.fad_fmn_cofactor_evidence: UniProt records FAD with experimental support from PMID:22267661 and PMID:6848481 and notes one FAD per subunit. The RCSB structures include FAD-bound and FAD/NADP-bound OTEMO coordinates.

nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.evidence: UniProt/Rhea records an NADPH/O2 reaction for the oxocyclopentenylacetyl-CoA substrate. The OTEMO structural paper describes type I BVMOs as noncovalently bound FAD enzymes reduced by NADPH before oxygen activation.
nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.two_component_distinction: This source context is not the FMN/NADH type II camphor BVMO system; OTEMO is the type I FAD/NADPH oxygenase and is not a separate reductase-only component.

candidate_packets.o2_derived_substrate_oxygen_insertion_ev: UniProt/Rhea records lactonization/oxygen insertion into the CoA-activated oxocyclopentenyl substrate. The open OTEMO paper describes the accepted BVMO catalytic cycle: NADPH reduction of FAD, reaction with O2 to a flavin-peroxide intermediate, attack on ketone substrate, Criegee intermediate formation, and lactone product formation.

duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:131: low direct reaction duplicate risk; OTEMO is BVMO oxygen insertion, not aromatic hydroxylation. Prior local terminal packet nevertheless recorded current-countable structural duplicate/leakage risk outside this source pass.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:132: low direct chemistry duplicate; OTEMO is FAD/NADPH type I BVMO, not FMNH2 alkanal luciferase chemistry.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:551: low direct chemistry duplicate; not phenol hydroxylation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:973: low direct chemistry duplicate; not two-component sulfur monooxygenation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.external_family_overlap: High broad-family overlap with CHMO and HAPMO. Prior local source-free terminal evidence recorded duplicate/leakage and generic flavin-redox scoring risk for H3JQW0.

not_other_family_rationale.not_ordinary_flavin_dehydrogenase_reduct: The source reaction is lactone-forming oxygen insertion rather than substrate dehydrogenation.
not_other_family_rationale.not_oxidase_only: The reaction summary accounts for O2-derived oxygen in the substrate product and water as the second oxygen fate.
not_other_family_rationale.not_fe_s_relay_or_reductase_only: No Fe-S relay or separate reductase-only role is supported; the reviewed entry is the FAD/NADPH oxygenating enzyme.
not_other_family_rationale.not_heme_p450_pterin_metal_copper: Sources identify FAD/NADPH BVMO chemistry and FAD/NADP structures, not heme, P450, pterin, non-heme iron, copper, or diiron oxygenation.
not_other_family_rationale.not_name_only: The evidence includes reviewed UniProt/Rhea reaction, FAD/NADP structural coordinates, and BVMO flavin-peroxide/Criegee mechanism discussion.

candidate_packets.disposition_reason: Source evidence is strong FMO evidence, but prior source-free terminal duplicate/leakage context and same-BVMO-lane redundancy make this a boundary hold rather than a clean new geometry lead in this pass.

candidate_packets.fad_fmn_cofactor_evidence: UniProt records FAD as cofactor with experimental support from PMID:11322873 and notes one FAD per subunit. PMID:11322873 reports purified HAPMO as a homodimer with each subunit containing noncovalently bound FAD.

nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.evidence: UniProt/Rhea records an NADPH/O2 reaction. PMID:11322873 characterizes HAPMO as an NADPH-dependent flavoprotein with tight coupling between NADPH oxidation and substrate oxygenation. PMID:16049018 supports persistent nicotinamide coenzyme binding during catalysis.
nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.two_component_distinction: No separate partner reductase or reduced-FMN donor is invoked; HAPMO is a single-component FAD/NADPH BVMO.

candidate_packets.o2_derived_substrate_oxygen_insertion_ev: UniProt records Baeyer-Villiger insertion of oxygen into a carbon-carbon bond adjacent to a carbonyl, converting ketones to esters. PMID:11322873 describes HAPMO-catalyzed Baeyer-Villiger rearrangement to phenyl acetates. The open HAPMO paper places HAPMO in the BVMO mechanism class where enzyme-bound flavin reacts with NAD(P)H and O2 to generate a peroxyflavin intermediate for carbonyl attack.

duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:131: low; HAPMO is aryl-ketone BVMO ester formation, not aromatic ring hydroxylation of 4-hydroxybenzoate.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:132: low; HAPMO is FAD/NADPH type I BVMO, not FMNH2 alkanal luciferase chemistry.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:551: low; HAPMO is carbonyl oxygen insertion, not phenol ortho hydroxylation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:973: low; HAPMO is not a two-component FMNH2 sulfur monooxygenase.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.external_family_overlap: Broad BVMO family overlap with CHMO and OTEMO. It remains useful as an aryl-ketone/HAPMO source lead but should not be counted as a separate diversity axis from BVMO alone.

not_other_family_rationale.not_ordinary_flavin_dehydrogenase_reduct: The product is an oxygen-inserted ester, not a redox-pair dehydrogenation product.
not_other_family_rationale.not_oxidase_only: HAPMO couples NADPH oxidation to substrate oxygenation rather than uncoupled oxidase turnover.
not_other_family_rationale.not_fe_s_relay_or_reductase_only: No Fe-S relay, reduced-flavin shuttle, or reductase-only component is supported in the reviewed source context.
not_other_family_rationale.not_heme_p450_pterin_metal_copper: Sources identify an FAD/NADPH BVMO with no heme, P450, pterin, metal, or copper oxygenase evidence.
not_other_family_rationale.not_name_only: Evidence includes reviewed UniProt/Rhea reaction, experimental FAD binding, NADPH dependence, and BVMO peroxyflavin mechanism context.

candidate_packets.disposition_reason: Strong source evidence, reviewed UniProt/Rhea support, and low direct duplicate risk against the current M-CSA FMO rows. Carry forward only to later source-free geometry and review-packet gates.

rhea.reaction: hypotaurine + NADPH + O2 + H(+) = taurine + NADP(+) + H2O
hypotaurine + NADH + O2 + H(+) = taurine + NAD(+) + H2O
trimethylamine + NADPH + O2 = trimethylamine N-oxide + NADP(+) + H2O
N,N-dimethylaniline + NADPH + O2 + H(+) = N,N-dimethylaniline N-oxide + NADP(+) + H2O

candidate_packets.fad_fmn_cofactor_evidence: UniProt records FAD as FMO1 cofactor with experimental evidence from PMID:32156684. PMID:34509493 identifies human FMO1 as using FAD and NADPH as cofactors and directly studies the hFMO1 flavin intermediate.

nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.evidence: UniProt/Rhea records NADPH-dependent dimethylaniline and trimethylamine N-oxygenation reactions and both NADPH- and NADH-supported hypotaurine oxygenation. PMID:32156684 confirms human FMO1 converts hypotaurine to taurine using either NADPH or NADH in vitro.
nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.two_component_distinction: FMO1 is a single polypeptide class B flavin-containing monooxygenase; the source evidence does not describe a partner reductase or reduced-flavin supply system.

candidate_packets.o2_derived_substrate_oxygen_insertion_ev: UniProt records N- and S/soft-nucleophile oxygenation reactions with O2 and nicotinamide reductant. PMID:34509493 demonstrates formation of a highly stable C4a-hydroperoxyflavin intermediate of human FMO1 after NADPH reduction in the presence of O2 and reports tight coupling in the presence of substrate. PMID:7217103 supplies the classic FMO oxidative-half-reaction evidence for stable C4a-hydroperoxyflavin chemistry.

substrate_product_reaction_summary.cosubstrates_products: NADPH or NADH + O2 -> NADP(+) or NAD(+) + H2O

duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:131: low; human FMO1 N/S or soft-nucleophile oxygenation is distinct from aromatic hydroxylation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:132: low; FMO1 is class B FAD/NAD(P)H FMO rather than an FMNH2 alkanal luciferase oxygenase.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:551: low; FMO1 is not phenol aromatic hydroxylation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:973: partial reaction-theme overlap for sulfur oxygenation, but low duplicate risk because FMO1 is a single-chain class B FAD/NAD(P)H FMO while DszC is a two-component reduced-FMN sulfur monooxygenase.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.external_family_overlap: Unique mammalian class B FMO lane among the six candidates.

not_other_family_rationale.not_ordinary_flavin_dehydrogenase_reduct: NADPH/NADH reduces the flavin to generate an oxygenating C4a-hydroperoxyflavin; the substrate receives oxygen rather than undergoing simple dehydrogenation.
not_other_family_rationale.not_oxidase_only: FMO1 source data support oxygenated substrate products and low uncoupling in the presence of substrate, not O2 terminal acceptor chemistry only.
not_other_family_rationale.not_fe_s_relay_or_reductase_only: No Fe-S relay or partner reductase-only system is involved; oxygen activation is by enzyme-bound FAD.
not_other_family_rationale.not_heme_p450_pterin_metal_copper: The enzyme is explicitly FMO/FAD chemistry and is separate from heme P450, pterin, metal, and copper oxygenases.
not_other_family_rationale.not_name_only: Evidence includes reviewed UniProt/Rhea reactions and direct human FMO1 C4a-hydroperoxyflavin source support.

candidate_packets.disposition_reason: Strong, candidate-specific human FMO1 evidence for FAD/NAD(P)H/O2 C4a-hydroperoxyflavin oxygenation and low duplicate risk against existing FMO rows. Carry forward only to later source-free geometry/review work.

rhea.reaction: L-kynurenine + NADPH + O2 + H(+) = 3-hydroxy-L-kynurenine + NADP(+) + H2O

candidate_packets.fad_fmn_cofactor_evidence: UniProt records FAD as KMO cofactor with evidence from PMID:10672018 and PMID:29429898. PMID:10672018 reports recombinant human KMO contains one noncovalently bound FAD per enzyme molecule. RCSB PDB 5X68 is the human KMO crystal structure and includes FAD.

nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.evidence: UniProt/Rhea records the NADPH/O2 hydroxylation of L-kynurenine to 3-hydroxy-L-kynurenine. PMID:9237672 and PMID:10672018 characterize human KMO as an NADPH-dependent flavin monooxygenase.
nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.two_component_distinction: No partner reductase or reduced-flavin shuttle is indicated; KMO is a single oxygenating flavoenzyme rather than a reductase-only system.

candidate_packets.o2_derived_substrate_oxygen_insertion_ev: UniProt/Rhea records O2-dependent hydroxylation of L-kynurenine. The KMO structural source in PMCID:PMC3736096 describes the natural catalytic cycle as involving a flavin C4a hydroperoxide/C4a peroxide intermediate and places the substrate C3 atom adjacent to the flavin C4a peroxide in the proposed hydroxylation model.

duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:131: high; prior local source-free terminal packet found a high-TM duplicate/leakage signal against canonical m_csa:131 / pdb:1DOC, and both are FAD/NADPH aromatic hydroxylase-like FMO rows.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:132: low direct chemistry duplicate; KMO is not FMNH2 alkanal luciferase chemistry.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:551: moderate to high family overlap; KMO and phenol 2-monooxygenase both support FAD/NAD(P)H aromatic hydroxylation through oxygenating flavin chemistry.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:973: low; KMO aromatic hydroxylation is distinct from reduced-FMN sulfur oxygenation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.external_family_overlap: Same broad aromatic hydroxylase lane as salicylate 1-monooxygenase and current m_csa:131/m_csa:551 support.

not_other_family_rationale.not_ordinary_flavin_dehydrogenase_reduct: The source reaction is hydroxylation of L-kynurenine, not substrate dehydrogenation or carrier reduction.
not_other_family_rationale.not_oxidase_only: The product is hydroxylated substrate, and KMO source context discusses peroxide intermediate placement for hydroxylation rather than only H2O2 formation.
not_other_family_rationale.not_fe_s_relay_or_reductase_only: No Fe-S relay or partner-only reductase source evidence is present.
not_other_family_rationale.not_heme_p450_pterin_metal_copper: Reviewed source context identifies FAD/NADPH KMO, not heme/P450, pterin, non-heme iron, copper, or diiron oxygenation.
not_other_family_rationale.not_name_only: Evidence includes reviewed UniProt/Rhea reaction, experimental FAD/NADPH support, human KMO structure, and C4a peroxide/hydroperoxide mechanism context.

candidate_packets.disposition_reason: Source chemistry is strong FMO evidence, but prior duplicate/leakage against m_csa:131 and aromatic-hydroxylase family overlap block clean progression in this acquisition pass.

rhea.reaction: salicylate + NADH + O2 + 2 H(+) = catechol + CO2 + NAD(+) + H2O

pdb.title: Structure and mechanism of salicylate hydroxylase from Pseudomonas putida G7
pdb.cofactor_coordinate_note: RCSB nonpolymer entities retrieved for 6BZ5 did not include FAD, so this pass treats FAD support as source/literature evidence rather than a holo-coordinate claim.

candidate_packets.fad_fmn_cofactor_evidence: UniProt records FAD as the cofactor. PMID:34965488/PMCID:PMC8824312 states that salicylate hydroxylase NahG has a single redox site where FAD is reduced by NADH and reports kinetic/product studies of intact FAD and FAD pieces.

nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.evidence: UniProt/Rhea records NADH, O2, and salicylate conversion to catechol, CO2, NAD(+), and water. PMCID:PMC8824312 describes FAD reduction by NADH in the same redox site before O2 activation.
nadph_nadh_or_reduced_flavin_supply_evid.two_component_distinction: This is a one-component FAD/NADH monooxygenase; no partner reductase or diffusible reduced FMN/FAD supply is required in the source evidence.

candidate_packets.o2_derived_substrate_oxygen_insertion_ev: PMID:34965488/PMCID:PMC8824312 states that O2 is activated by reduced flavin and salicylate undergoes oxidative decarboxylation by a C4a-hydroperoxyflavin intermediate to give catechol. UniProt/Rhea records the salicylate + NADH + O2 oxidative decarboxylation reaction.

duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:131: moderate to high family overlap; both are FAD-dependent aromatic hydroxylase/decarboxylating hydroxylase-like rows using reduced flavin plus O2.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:132: low; salicylate 1-monooxygenase is FAD/NADH aromatic oxidative decarboxylation, not FMNH2 alkanal luciferase chemistry.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:551: moderate to high family overlap; both support phenolic/aromatic hydroxylation through C4a-hydroperoxyflavin chemistry.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.m_csa:973: low; salicylate hydroxylation/decarboxylation is distinct from two-component sulfur oxygenation.
duplicate_risk_against_existing_mcsa.external_family_overlap: Same broad aromatic hydroxylase lane as KMO and current m_csa:131/m_csa:551 support; useful corroboration but not a clean new axis in this pass.

not_other_family_rationale.not_ordinary_flavin_dehydrogenase_reduct: The source reaction is oxidative decarboxylation to catechol through C4a-hydroperoxyflavin, not simple hydride-transfer dehydrogenation.
not_other_family_rationale.not_oxidase_only: The source explicitly partitions C4a-hydroperoxyflavin toward salicylate hydroxylation, not only peroxide-forming oxidase turnover.
not_other_family_rationale.not_fe_s_relay_or_reductase_only: No Fe-S relay or partner reductase-only source role is present; FAD reduction and O2 activation occur in NahG.
not_other_family_rationale.not_heme_p450_pterin_metal_copper: The evidence identifies FAD/NADH flavoprotein chemistry and no heme, P450, pterin, metal, or copper oxygenase requirement.
not_other_family_rationale.not_name_only: Evidence includes reviewed UniProt/Rhea reaction and an explicit source for C4a-hydroperoxyflavin oxidative decarboxylation.

candidate_packets.disposition_reason: Strong FMO-positive source evidence, but same-family aromatic hydroxylase overlap with m_csa:131 and m_csa:551 makes it corroborative rather than a clean new source-free geometry lead in this pass.

Keep uniprot:H3JQW0 and uniprot:O15229 on source_boundary_hold unless a future explicit user request reopens their prior duplicate/leakage terminal context.
